title: Housing
summary: ## House and home; functions of a home

A house is a physical construction of brick, sand, cement and stone; it becomes a home when family members live there and carry out health, ease, comfort, social and entertainment activities. A home has protective (security, protection from weather, animals and enemies), economic (value in money, raises socio-economic status, gives pride, can host income-generating activity such as tuitions or a paying guest), educative (basic values, life skills such as sharing and caring) and social/religious functions (interaction within and outside the family, belongingness, passing values and customs down the generations; celebrating festivals).

The site is the place where a house is built. Consider: neighbourhood – a developed area with electricity, roads and drainage and nearby post office, bank, school and market; physical features – open area, away from heavy traffic (air and noise pollution), avoid low-lying land (flooding and water-logging), elevated sites give a better view and drain water; soil – firm 2–5 feet below the surface for a strong foundation, loose soil makes the house tilt, sandy and gravelly soils make it hot, rocky surface is good for foundation but does not absorb water and complicates laying drainage pipes; sanitary requirements – avoid garbage-filled plots (uneven level, drainage problems), fill with fresh firm soil and raise to road level; practical convenience – market, transport, post office, bank and hospital within reasonable walking distance.

Make a list of activities in each room and mark space for each; combine activities (dining with kitchen or drawing room, study with bedroom); do not overcrowd; use multipurpose furniture (sofa-cum-bed, dining table for study), furniture as room dividers and storage, space under the staircase for a store or toilet. Living room: for entertaining guests, relaxation and reading; near the entrance; furniture arranged so that people can talk; good lighting. Bedroom: privacy, free from noise, rectangular shape is convenient, preferably attached to a bathroom (we spend about one-third of life sleeping). Bathroom: bathing space, water closet and wash area; non-slippery, easy-to-clean floor; at least one wall exposed to the outside for light and air. Kitchen: ideally in the east or north-east to get morning sunlight (a disinfectant), good drainage, wire-mesh doors, adequate day and night lighting, one wall on the exterior, exhaust fan, cross ventilation, storage above and below the counter, light-coloured walls.

Natural light (sun) is important for all rooms, especially kitchen and bathrooms; without sun they stay dark and damp, attract mosquitoes and cockroaches and increase infections and fungal diseases. Artificial light should fall on the work, not in the eyes; glare causes eye ache. Ventilation circulates fresh air and drives out stale air through windows, ventilators and exhaust fans; keep at least one window open even in winter; cross ventilation by windows on two sides or a door and window opposite each other; openings at floor level bring in fresh air and those near the ceiling drive out stale air. Sanitation covers cleanliness, removal of garbage and disposal of waste water and excreta.

Cleaning is daily (sweeping, mopping, dusting, making beds, tidying, cleaning rugs), weekly (bathrooms, toilets, washbasins, cobwebs, shelves, door handles, polishing wood) and seasonal or spring cleaning (airing mattresses, washing curtains, cleaning the store room and woodwork, thorough cleaning before Diwali). Start daily cleaning from the innermost part after making beds, open windows, sweep with a soft broom, dust, brush carpets and mop with phenyl. Use indoor footwear and foot mats; fine wire mesh keeps out dust and insects. Materials: floors – broom, soap, kerosene, phenyl; tiles – soap, vinegar, mild hydrochloric acid; plastic buckets and mugs – lukewarm soap solution, vinegar, soda (no hard cleaners); glass and mirrors – moist newspaper, vinegar; metal and brass taps – lemon, vinegar, tamarind, salt; wood – soft cloth wrung from mild soap solution.

Garbage: collect in a covered dustbin, empty daily into the public bin; segregate bio-degradable (peels) from non-bio-degradable (plastic); in villages bury bio-degradable waste in a pit to make manure. Waste water goes by drain to a kitchen garden or soakage pit, never left to stagnate. Soakage pit: about 2 m deep, 1 m wide and 2–3 m long, one-third filled with coarse stones, then small stones and pebbles, then sand, covered with earth and grass; not built near a well; needs no drainage system. Human excreta: water closet (most sanitary, needs plenty of water and is expensive); septic tank (Sulabh Shauchalaya; hygienic, low cost, no pollution of surface or ground water, no foul smell, needs only 1.5–2 litres of water for flushing against 13–14 litres in a flush toilet, no cleaning of pits, sludge is good manure, prevents mosquitoes and flies); pit latrine (more than 3 m deep, sandy soil, covered; temporary use, can pollute ground water).

objective: Fill in the blanks: (i) Besides windows, doors and ventilators, ______ should be installed in the kitchen to remove stale air. (ii) Chances of infections and fungal diseases increase if the rooms are ______. (iii) The floor of a bathroom should be ______. (iv) The living room should be near the ______ of the building.
(i) an exhaust fan. (ii) dark and damp. (iii) non-slippery. (iv) entrance.

State True or False: (i) Removing cobwebs is a daily activity. (ii) Safe disposal of excreta helps to keep our environment healthy. (iii) Cross ventilation is achieved by placing two windows on opposite walls. (iv) A rocky surface is good for the foundation of a house as it absorbs water.
(i) False – it is a weekly activity. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – rocky surface is good for the foundation but does not absorb water.

Fill in the blanks: (i) Besides sanitation, two other aspects of maintaining hygiene in houses are ______ and ______. (ii) To make your house more spacious combine the kitchen with ______ and ______ room.

vsa: Write any four educational functions of a house.

It teaches basic values like respect for elders, love and affection, religion, discipline and responsibility; life skills like sharing, caring and empathy; health habits; and transfers customs and values from generation to generation.
October 2025

or: List any four household activities that are done once a week in your home.
Cleaning bathrooms and toilets; removing cobwebs; cleaning kitchen shelves; cleaning door handles; polishing wooden surfaces; cleaning washbasins and metal objects.

vsa: Analyse any two common mistakes in selecting a bedroom.
Choosing a noisy room with no privacy; an odd shape that cannot hold beds and furniture; no attached bathroom; poor light and ventilation.
What two points each should be considered while making a bathroom and bedroom?
Bathroom: non-slippery easy-to-clean floor; at least one wall exposed to the outside for light and air. Bedroom: privacy and freedom from noise; rectangular shape; attached bathroom.
April 2025

or: What is the ideal direction for a kitchen? What other three aspects should be considered while making it?
East or north-east for morning sunlight. Also: good drainage and wire-mesh doors, adequate light and exhaust fan with cross ventilation, adequate storage above and below the counter.

vsa: Apart from soap and water, what materials are used for washing tiles, plastic buckets and metal taps in the bathroom?
Tiles: commercial tile cleaners, vinegar, mild hydrochloric acid. Plastic buckets: scrubber, vinegar, kerosene and soda (avoid hard cleaners). Metal taps: lemon, vinegar, tamarind and salt.
April 2024
Why is it important to ensure enough light and air circulation in a house? Give two reasons each.

Light: kills germs and keeps rooms dry so mosquitoes and fungus do not breed; helps in work and prevents eye strain. Air: removes smoke, smell and moisture; fresh air is essential for health and prevents stuffiness.
October 2022
Why is cleanliness of the house and its surroundings important?
Clean surroundings keep insects and germs away; dust spreads diseases; it prevents infections, saves the house from damage and makes it pleasant to live in.
October 2022
Suggest two ways of making provisions for light in a house.
Provide windows, ventilators and skylights so that most rooms get sunlight; use proper artificial lighting (tube light, bulbs) that falls on the work and not on the eyes.
April 2023
sa: What are six advantages of making a toilet based on septic tanks?

It is hygienic; low cost and easy to construct compared with the water-closet system; does not pollute surface or ground water; free from foul smell; needs only 1.5–2 litres of water for flushing against 13–14 litres in a flush toilet; needs no cleaning of pits and the sludge is good manure; also eliminates mosquitoes, insects and fly breeding.

or: What six points should be kept in mind to ensure the rooms in your house do not get dirty?

Use special indoor footwear and foot mats; fit fine wire mesh on doors and windows; keep things in their places; do daily, weekly and seasonal cleaning properly; keep dustbins covered and empty them daily; avoid bringing in dust, and dispose of waste water and garbage properly.

sa: Analyse any six possible mistakes families make while selecting a bedroom.

Choosing a room that is noisy or lacks privacy; badly lit or poorly ventilated; too small or odd-shaped to place beds and furniture; far from the bathroom; near the kitchen or the entrance; ignoring storage; too much furniture; not considering that one-third of life is spent sleeping.
Write any six features on the basis of which you will select the site for your new house.

Developed neighbourhood with electricity, roads and drainage; open area away from heavy traffic; not low-lying (no flooding or water-logging); firm soil 2–5 feet below the surface; not a garbage-filled plot; markets, transport, bank, post office and hospital within walking distance; matching the family's social and economic status.

or: Give six suggestions to make your house more comfortable.

List activities of each room and mark space; combine activities (dining with kitchen); avoid overcrowding; use multipurpose furniture; use furniture for storage and as room dividers; use space below the staircase; light colours on walls; ensure light and ventilation.

la: Explain the functions of a home with examples (any five points).

(1) Protective: gives security and shelter from weather, animals and enemies. (2) Economic: has a money value, raises socio-economic status and pride, and can be used for income-generating activity (tuitions, paying guest). (3) Educative: teaches values such as respect and discipline and life skills like sharing and caring. (4) Social/religious: promotes interaction within and outside the family and a sense of belongingness. (5) Transfers values and customs from generation to generation, celebrates festivals together.
Describe the methods of safe disposal of human excreta in villages and towns.

Water closet: excreta carried by flush through drains and sewers, the most sanitary but needs plenty of water and is expensive. Septic tank: concrete tank connected to household drains, hygienic, low cost, needs only 1.5–2 litres of water, no foul smell, sludge is manure (Sulabh Shauchalaya). Pit latrine: pit more than 3 m deep in sandy soil with a lid, for temporary use; not very hygienic because it can pollute ground water. Soakage pits take waste water where no drainage exists.
